question: Should OpenClaw define an opt-in generic adaptive inbound debounce contract now, keep fixed debounce as the supported behavior, or defer smarter timing to a channel/plugin seam first?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes how inbound fragments become agent turns, so automation cannot safely choose increment/max defaults, count-trigger semantics, typing-signal trust, transcript shape, or rollout policy.

options.title: Design one opt-in adaptive contract
options.body: Add a single generic inbound debounce policy with explicit initial/increment/max or equivalent semantics, plus schema, docs, and representative channel tests.

options.title: Keep fixed debounce only
options.body: Document messages.inbound.debounceMs/byChannel and queue modes as the supported batching answer, then close smarter timing requests as not planned.

options.title: Require a channel/plugin seam first
options.body: Defer core config until a typed channel or plugin ingress hook can expose provider-specific typing or count signals without growing global message config.

recommendation.title: Design one opt-in adaptive contract
recommendation.body: Add a single generic inbound debounce policy with explicit initial/increment/max or equivalent semantics, plus schema, docs, and representative channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across the shared inbound debounce policy and ordering fixes that this product/API choice would affect.
